properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-07, dev_reflow2 hub, right after the one-graph requirement was recorded: "this linking of similar things may need to be considered on the 'one design', even though there may be in actuality, multiple individual design projects/repos. This may also help prevent duplicate decisions/ideas/requirements/capabilities or issues in proper separation of concerns."

WHERE IT STANDS: linking (the brainstorm and link-ideas skills, relation_candidates, review_relations) works inside one design only. An edge cannot cross a store. The /hub skill's own honest limit says it: "A pointer in the hub is text, not an edge." So a requirement in flo2 that DUPLICATES one in reflow2, or a decision in integrated-flo that CONTRADICTS one in flo2-cad, can be written down only as prose, which no detector, suggester or search reads as a relation. Slice 2 added the first typed cross-design reference: a pin's `interfaces`, read by the ripple.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) PROSE ONLY, as today. Free. Invisible to every check.
(b) A CROSS-DESIGN RELATION RECORD in the design that cites the other: the relation type, this node, and the other node's id plus the other design's id. A new node type or a new Resource kind, read by link-ideas, the duplicate warning and the ripple. Medium. Each design stays readable alone, and the far end may not exist or may move, so a check reports dangling or moved links, as the dependency watch does.
(c) THE HUB HOLDS THE CROSS-LINKS between its members' nodes. Small to start, but it puts members' facts in the hub, against the one-home rule, and is useless where there is no hub.
(d) THE HOST (flo2.io) HOLDS THEM, alongside dec:idea-flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-design-graph-when-asked in flo2's design. Only for hosted designs.

COUNTERPOINTS:
- Relatedness is a judgement, and across designs written in different words it is harder; the 2026-09-22 ruling made the duplicate warning advisory for exactly that reason. A wrong cross-design link is worse than a missing one.
- The suggester is already weak inside one design (fact:root-cause-idea-linking-covers-open-ideas-in-pairs-and-a-vision-spread-across-requirements-is-never-gathered-2026-10-07: same-type pool, author-dominated). Widening it across designs before fixing it would multiply noise.

CHEAPEST REAL STEP: fix the suggester and widen it to requirements inside one design first (F1, F2, F5 of that root cause). Then (b) for the cross-design case.



═══ SETTLED 2026-10-07 — OPTION (b) ═══
Anthony, 2026-10-07, asked for the agent's recommendation on the four open choices and replied "Go with your picks". The pick: (b), a cross-design relation record kept in the design that makes the link. It carries the relation, this node, the other design's id and the node id there, and a check reports a far end that is missing or has moved. Why (b): the duplicate warning, a recorded duplicate, slice 3's move-or-decompose and the root-cause neighbours pass all need a typed pointer into another design. (c) hub-held lost because it puts members' facts in the hub against the one-home rule and does not exist without a hub. (d) host-held lost because it serves flo2.io only, not Anthony's or Alex's work. (a) prose lost because no check reads it.

═══ 2026-10-10 — @ajs ASKS WHAT A HUB IS AT THE STORE LEVEL. RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING; the settlement above stands unless he reopens it. ═══
In his words: "at the reflow2 level and specifically at what actually gets stored in rocksdb, I believe that each design has a 'design_id' or something like that. When we create a hub of a design, are we now linking at a hub level: design_id_1, design_id_2, ..., design_id_n? I think at the reflow2 level, each design is a set of key:values (like in the rocksdb or BTreeMap level). If we linked two or more designs, are we effectively just concatenating all of key:values for design 1 + key:values for design 2 + key:values for design n and basically allow them to be treated as one single set of key:values?"

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY: each design is one store with one graph_id (graph.id.json beside it); node and edge keys inside a store carry no design id, because a store holds one design. A hub is a design whose pins name other designs by graph_id (external_dependency with `graph_id`, and on flo2.io the host's member list). Nothing is concatenated: an edge cannot cross a store, and a relation into another design is a typed REFERENCE node here (`xref:<graph_id>:<node_id>`, option b above) that stands in for the far node and is checked against it. A design stays readable, exportable and backed up on its own.

THREE WAYS "ONE SET OF KEY:VALUES" COULD BE TRUE, none chosen:
(a) STORED UNION: the family lives in one store, every key prefixed by its design's graph_id. One search, one walk, one gap pass over everything, for free. AGAINST: one store is one single-writer lock, one backup, one blast radius and one membership for N designs, which is what the one-blueprint and tiered-reach settlements keep apart; a member's owner could not take their design away; and flo2.io's registry already holds every store in one process without merging them.
(b) ASSEMBLED UNION, WHEN ASKED: the stores stay apart; an analysis opens the N stores (or exports) and reads them as one graph for one question, with each node still knowing its design. This EXISTS locally as compose_and_analyse (crates/reflow2-core/src/compose.rs), which composes designs by path, and is withheld on flo2.io because a hosted design opens nothing by path; flo2's dec:idea-flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-design-graph-when-asked is the hosted version, where the host, which holds every store, assembles for the caller. One-graph behaviour without one-graph storage.
(c) TYPED LINKS ONLY, as settled on 2026-10-07: each design keeps references to the others, and the hub work (send down, ripple member to member, one search across members) hops from store to store. The family reads as one graph through the links, never as one set of keys.

A RANKING IS A FINDING: (c) is built and in use; (b) is built locally and open on flo2.io; (a) would undo three settlements for a convenience (b) gives without them. What (a) alone would answer: a key:value question that spans designs in one lock, which nothing today needs.

2026-10-10, END OF THE BRAINSTORM: @ajs kept (b), assembled when asked, and not (a). The settlement above (typed links, stores apart) stands. The local half exists (compose_and_analyse, req:composed-analysis); the hosted half is now flo2's accepted req:flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-graph-when-asked. No change to reflow2's store: a design is one store with one graph_id, and a hub names others by graph_id.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-07 — a relation between nodes in two designs is a typed link record kept in the design that makes it (option b)
properties.rationale: Anthony's aim is a set of designs worked as one design graph (req:a-set-of-designs-that-make-up-one-system-is-worked-as-one-design-graph). Linking is how a graph keeps related things findable together, and today it stops at each design's edge.
